title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (10-20Y nominal, 1:40pm ET) — last of the doubled-size window
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-06 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35) — the row reads verbatim announce 11/3/2026, operation 11/4/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 11/5/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 10Y to 20Y, maturity range 11/05/2036 - 11/04/2046, min $0, max $2 billion. Stays estimate on three counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, its $2B cap is SUPERSEDED (see notes), and the confirming primary is the 11-03 operation announcement rather than this document, checked 2026-09-06
notes: THE PUBLISHED CAP ON THIS ROW IS STALE AND SHOULD NOT BE QUOTED. Press release sb0607 (2026-08-19) raises the long-end (10-20Y and 20-30Y) maximum from '$2 billion per operation' to 'at least $4 billion per operation', 'effective September 9, 2026 and ... in effect for the remainder of this refunding quarter (through November 4, 2026)', so the operative cap here is at least $4B. Why it earns a slot: this is the LAST long-end operation inside the doubled-size window — it falls on 2026-11-04 itself, the window's stated end date and the Quarterly Refunding date at which sb0607 says 'Treasury will provide more information about future buyback sizes'. That makes it the terminal test of the program treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 tracks, and it shares its date with treasury-refunding-2026-11-04 (est) and treasury-borrowing-estimates-2026-11-02's follow-on, which is exactly what will make this operation's own tape effect unmeasurable. SHARPENED BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-06): whether the doubled cap still applies is settled on 11-03, NOT on the day. Schedule footnote 1 puts the announcement — and therefore the published maximum — at 11:00am ET on the Announcement Date, which is 11/3/2026; the Quarterly Refunding statement that sets every LATER cap posts 08:30 ET on 11-04, five hours before the 1:40pm operation. So this operation runs under a number already fixed and cannot be resized by the statement sharing its date; forward-sizing findings belong on treasury-refunding-2026-11-04, not here. Two measured facts from fiscaldata buybacks_operations (128 rows, pulled direct 2026-09-06): 10Y-20Y liquidity support has filled its announced cap in 25 of 25 operations, but only 13 of 41 $4B-capped operations across all sectors fill, so full fill is a sector property rather than a programme one; and exactly two operations have ever landed on a refunding-statement day — 2026-02-04 (1Mo-2Y, full fill) and 2026-05-06 (10Y-20Y, $19.69B offered, above the 2026 median, full fill), an exact matched control against the 'bidders stand aside' worry. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and a $0-4B liquidity-support operation is a demand-side mechanic, not a price signal. Discovered during the treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-06); the same schedule's 11-05 1Mo-2Y operation sits outside the long-end sectors this event covers and is deliberately NOT filed here.
